00Summary at a Glance

Current read: wait-and-see bias · re-assess after earnings
Sandisk sits in a classic peak-cycle debate: record profits at a P/E of 7x as NAND prices surge. FADU has just emerged from losses and is at the start of a growth phase, but its price already reflects a distant future. In one day FADU fell more than 9%, giving back over half of its September rebound. Both companies report within 3 to 4 weeks (Oct 29 and Nov 12), so the analysis favors a staged approach: re-assess after the earnings conditions are confirmed.
  • The fundamental picture is positive. Sandisk's latest quarter: revenue of $8.97 bn (+372% year on year) and a gross margin of 84.6%. FADU turned profitable in Q1 2026, posted operating profit of KRW 16.2 bn in Q2, and Q3 consensus is KRW 33.7 bn.
  • Valuation pressure runs in opposite directions. Sandisk trades at 6.9x next-fiscal-year estimated P/E; FADU at about 61x 2026E P/E and 52x P/B.
  • Timing is unfavorable. Sandisk is down 10.7% over 5 trading days and, although the Oct 13 decline narrowed to -0.34%, sits below its 20-, 60- and 120-day moving averages. FADU fell 9.18% on Oct 14 alone and 23.8% over 5 days, lost its 60-day MA, and closed below the opens of both September base candles.
  • Next checkpoints. Oct 22 Bank of Korea rate decision (MPC); Oct 28 FOMC and SK hynix Q3 earnings; Oct 29 Sandisk FY27 Q1 earnings; Nov 12 FADU Q3 earnings; and the ongoing trial tied to FADU's IPO.

01Who Makes What

Both are grouped under the "NAND/SSD" theme, but they do different things. Sandisk is a manufacturer that makes NAND chips itself. FADU is a fabless company that designs the controller, the brain of an SSD.

NAND makersSandisk (joint fabs with Kioxia), Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Micron
NAND chips
SSD controllersFADU (data-center focused), Marvell, Phison and others. Large makers also design in-house
Finished SSDs
Data centersHyperscalers such as Meta and Google, and server OEMs. Storage for AI training and inference data

Main customersHyperscalers, PC and smartphone makers, retail distributionUS big tech such as Meta and Google, new server OEMs
Current growth driverSurging NAND prices; data-center revenue (+103% quarter on quarter last quarter)Revenue ramp from the 2nd and 3rd hyperscalers; PCIe Gen6 controller

Is the "NAND supercycle" real?

In Sandisk's numbers, clearly yes. The catch is that two-thirds of the revenue increase came from price, which cuts both ways.

  • Price-led growth: Sandisk said about two-thirds of last quarter's revenue increase came from higher selling prices and one-third from shipments. TrendForce counted roughly a 100% rise in NAND prices in the first half; reports say contract prices will rise another 10-15% in Q3 but at a slower pace (the latter is a secondary report, original not verified).
  • How AI lifted NAND: Capacity shifting toward HBM created shortages across memory, and demand for high-capacity data-center SSDs for AI inference rose alongside.
  • What it means for FADU: More data-center SSD shipments mean more controller demand. However, FADU buys NAND for the SSD modules it sells, so surging NAND prices can become a cost burden.
  • Easy to overlook: FADU's earnings structure is only now being built. It has posted just two profitable quarters.

02Earnings and Outlook

Sandisk went from losses right after its spin-off to a company with $12.5 bn of operating profit in a year. FADU, after three straight loss-making years, is aiming for its first annual profit in 2026. Figures beyond the latest results are broker estimates.

Quarterly flow: how back-loaded is the second half?

About 74% of FADU's full-year estimate depends on the second half. First-half actual operating profit of KRW 23.9 bn must be joined by KRW 33.7 bn in Q3 and about KRW 35.3 bn in Q4 to reach KRW 92.9 bn. Eugene Investment & Securities expects Q3 operating profit of KRW 35.5 bn, above consensus, but the company's revenue fell sharply in the quarters right after its IPO, so whether the Nov 12 Q3 results match the estimates is the key checkpoint. Sandisk's gross margin last quarter was 84.6%, well above the top of guidance (79-81%); at the Oct 29 report the key items are whether NAND price increases continue and the terms of long-term supply agreements.

03How Rising NAND Prices Affect the Two Companies Differently

In the same NAND boom, Sandisk is the one that "gets the price" and FADU is the one that "follows the volume." That difference shows up in margins and in share-price volatility.

Sandisk: joined at the hip with Kioxia

  • NAND wafers are produced at joint fabs with Japan's Kioxia. Capacity expands more slowly than at rivals, so Sandisk captures much of the price effect in an upcycle.
  • Data-center revenue was $2.98 bn, about 33% of the total. A year ago, consumer and PC had a far larger share.
  • The shift to multi-year long-term supply agreements is the core of the bull case. The terms need to be checked at the Oct 29 report.

FADU: customer count is earnings

  • Brokers explain that after the first hyperscaler (reportedly Meta), revenue from a second customer is ramping and a third customer's revenue is starting to be recognized.
  • It recently won a new server OEM customer; it has shown a PCIe Gen6 controller and cited Gen7 development spending (completion of Gen6 development is not confirmed in public sources).
  • Competitors are large makers with their own controllers, such as Marvell, Phison and Samsung. Customers must re-qualify the product with each generation.

Net trading is listed in the order Oct 7, Oct 8, Oct 12, Oct 13, Oct 14 (the market was closed Oct 9). Jul 15 is the first day of the 60 trading days of data available. FADU's foreign ownership ratio fell 2.2 percentage points over three months. Foreigners kept net buying over the last 5 trading days, but Oct 14 was effectively neutral at +826 shares, and institutions turned to net selling of 76,995 shares that day, so their 20-day cumulative net buying shrank from 2.17 million shares in yesterday's report to 0.77 million. Retail investors net bought 77,980 shares the same day. Oct 14 volume of 454,314 shares was about 85% of the 20-day average (about 0.53 million), so the decline came on light trading rather than heavy panic selling. Sandisk is a US stock with no data in the same format, so we use volume instead. Its 20-day average of 8.54 million shares is below its 60-day average (12.34 million), suggesting a correction on shrinking volume rather than panic selling. Across the KOSPI market, foreigners net sold KRW 1.18 tn on Oct 14 (KRW 1,181.4 bn), a seventh straight day of net selling.

  • Rates: Rising long-term yields raise the funding cost of data-center investment and the discount rate on high-multiple stocks. Stocks at 60x P/E or more, like FADU, are the most sensitive to rates.
  • Indices: On Oct 14 KOSDAQ (−1.57%) fell more than KOSPI (−0.44%), and FADU (−9.18%) fell far more than either. FADU's drop looks more like stock-specific selling than an index move, but no stock-specific negative news was found. KOSPI barely held the 6,000 level, and forced liquidation of margin loans was the largest since Jul 31 (KRW 59.3 bn).
  • Relative strength: While KOSDAQ is down 4% over the year, FADU is up 179% and Sandisk is up 893%, more than ten times the SOX (+78.5%). The more a stock has risen, the larger the drawdown in a correction.

Conclusion
Uncertainty is too large to settle on a single judgment at this point. Sandisk is "cheap but in a peak debate"; FADU is "at the start of growth but expensive, with legal risk remaining." The analysis favors a staged approach for both: re-assess after the earnings reports due within 3 to 4 weeks. With FADU's chart signals weakening in a single day, this is one notch more conservative than yesterday's reading.
  • The good news lies in confirmed numbers. Sandisk's FY26 operating profit of $12.5 bn and FADU's first-half operating profit of KRW 23.9 bn are results, not forecasts.
  • The bad news is concentrated in this moment. Memory-sector weakness, US rates above 5% and worries about Chinese catch-up all landed in the same week. KOSPI failed to rebound on Oct 14 after falling 5.46% on Oct 13.
  • Between the two, Sandisk's price relative to earnings is overwhelmingly lower. But its profit is the quickest to shrink if NAND prices turn. FADU depends on customer-count expansion rather than NAND prices, so cycle sensitivity is lower, yet at 61x P/E even a small miss in Q3 results could mean a large drawdown.
  • Remaining uncertainty. It cannot yet be determined whether NAND prices hold through 2027, how FADU's trial will turn out, or whether FADU's 9% drop on Oct 14 had a stock-specific cause.

How the Dante technique is reflected. "Dante" is the pen name of 주식단테, a Korean stock YouTuber known for chart-based methods built on long moving averages and "base candles" (large high-volume candles that mark institutional accumulation). This report marks both Dante's 112-, 224- and 448-day averages and the 122-, 244- and 444-day averages requested for the report, and searches the daily bars directly for the signals Dante cites as evidence of "institutional accumulation," attaching a checklist for each stock. There are five criteria. ① Base candle (accumulation candle): a bullish candle with volume at least 2x the prior 20-day average and a body of 3% or more. ② Base candle open as support: whether later closes hold above that candle's open (in the Dante technique this open is treated as the big players' average cost and the reference for judging a breakdown). ③ Volume dry-up after the high-volume candle: how far the 10-day average volume after the base candle falls relative to the base candle. ④ Time correction below the 224-day MA: whether a "bowl pattern" second leg (sideways for four months or more) exists. ⑤ Suspected breakdown candle: a long bearish candle with at least 2x volume within 15% of the 52-week high. The ▲ markers and dotted lines on the chart show base candles within the last 150 trading days and their opens (orange = still holding, gray = already broken). These criteria were quantified from secondary sources that summarize the technique, not from Dante's original videos, so they may differ from Dante's own judgment.
